anomaly_def.Name: Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly : Concurrent sessions block or deadlock because they request incompatible locks on the same database resources.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database and related processes drive host CPU utilization to sustained saturation, starving other work of compute cycles.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : Client-server communication or connection-handling infrastructure becomes a bottleneck, producing slow or failed connects and stalled socket I/O.

When all three root causes manifest together, the database experiences compound distress: lock wait chains and deadlocks lengthen application response times; at the same time, CPU cores are fully subscribed by spin-loops, deadlock detection, and repeated statement retries; meanwhile, clients struggle to obtain or keep connections as the listener and socket queues overflow. Observable symptoms include: exploding lock-wait and deadlock counters, soaring host load averages and context-switch rates, widespread "CPU busy" or scheduler wait events, surging connection-attempt failures, elevated network retransmissions, and application timeouts that cannot easily be attributed to a single layer.

Causal interaction: Network slowdowns or connection slot exhaustion increase transaction round-trip latency, keeping transactions open longer and extending the interval during which they hold locks—thereby intensifying lock contention. Prolonged blocking chains induce repeated client retries and server-side deadlock detection, each consuming additional CPU and spawning more connection activity that further stresses the network stack. In parallel, near-maxed CPU resources lengthen lock acquisition and deadlock-resolution cycles, causing locks to persist even longer and amplifying contention. The escalating feedback loop among delayed network I/O, prolonged locks, and CPU saturation can quickly propagate through the workload, degrading throughput, inflating latency, and precipitating widespread application failures.

entry.official_description: Failed to establish MySQL client connection in Group Replication. Error establishing connection. Please refer to the manual to make sure that you configured Group Replication properly to work with MySQL Protocol connections.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with connection establishment, authentication exchange, protocol correctness, network reachability, or client/server communication stability.
entry.solution_guidance: Check endpoint reachability, authentication flow, connection limits, protocol compatibility, transport stability, and client connection lifecycle management.
